data.body: RCA progress 2026-09-08: Observation reproduced under controlled idle conditions in this worktree with TMPDIR routed to .rebar/tmp (no shared /tmp scratch): tests/interfaces/io/test_import_batch_resume.py::test_benchmark_commit_count_is_ceil_per_pass passed but took 268.13s, only ~32s below the repo-wide pytest-timeout 300s budget. Hypothesis H1: the fresh-store stall is not a malformed store or Gerrit/network dependency; it is deterministic per-event write publishability probing inside the batched importer. Experiment 1 (single variable: monkeypatch write_blocking_divergence to no-op for the same import shape): 50 CREATE+COMMENT records took 5.099s with the real probe versus 0.666s with only that probe removed; the real probe consumed 4.44s. Experiment 2 (single variable: count git calls while keeping behavior real): 10 CREATE+COMMENT records made 41 `git remote get-url origin` calls and 20 `git rev-parse --verify origin/tickets` calls, i.e. the supposedly batched import still pays two remote-url probes and one remote-ref probe per event before the batched commit. Idle 3000-record runtime scales from this per-event cost, so modest concurrent validation load pushes the benchmark over 300s and the timeout stack lands wherever the current git child is blocked (observed at `remote get-url origin`). H1 currently confirmed; next fix should preserve the write-divergence safety check but run it once per batch flush, not once per buffered event.
